title: [dkblinux98/nyxGPT] Feature: Add query result caching (#2687) (PR #3153)
medium: Cache not invalidated on collection re-index

minor: `src/nyxgpt/rag/rag.py:501,514`: `assert cache_key is not None` is used to satisfy type narrowing before `query_cache.set(...)`. This is logically guaranteed by the surrounding `if not collect_debug` structure, but asserts are stripped under `python -O`. Consider restructuring (e.g. an inline `if cache_key is not None:` guard, or extracting the whole "compute + cache" flow into a helper that takes a definite key) instead of relying on a strippable assert for correctness-relevant control flow. Low risk since this repo doesn't appear to run with `-O`, but worth a low-cost cleanup.

`_get_query_result_cache()` caches the backend instance (and its config-derived TTL/max_size/backend type) in a module-level global on first use, and `clear_query_cache()` only calls `.clear()` on the existing instance rather than re-reading config. If `[cache]` settings are changed via a runtime config reload (if such a mechanism exists elsewhere in the app), the new query-cache settings won't take effect without a process restart. This matches the existing pattern for the embedding/response caches, so it's not a regression introduced by this PR, just worth being aware of.

Cached results (`filtered`, a `list[dict]`) are stored and returned by reference from `MemoryCache`/`DiskCache.get()` rather than as a copy. I checked all current callers (`chat.py:600,609`, `app.py:2742`, `cli.py:812`) and none mutate the returned rows in place, so this isn't an active bug today — but a future caller that mutates a row dict in place (e.g. to enrich it) would silently corrupt the shared cached entry for all subsequent cache hits. Worth a one-line comment noting cached results must be treated as read-only, or defensively `copy.deepcopy`/shallow-copy on read if this becomes a concern.
